title: Progressive Degradation and Tenant Shaping for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Liam O'Connell
description: PRD for a progressive degradation system and per-tenant shaping controls for Dedicated capacity. Goal: keep tenant workloads live under constrained capacity by progressively degrading noncritical work, shaping bursts, and using transparent tenant-level policies so customers understand and control fallbacks.
problem_statement: During sustained load spikes and partial regional failures, Dedicated tenants either face hard failures (requests rejected) or opaque slowdowns that break downstream SLAs. Current reserved pool and burst handling focuses on admission and preemption but lacks a standardized, observable progressive degradation strategy that: (1) preserves core low-latency requests, (2) degrades noncritical work in controlled steps, and (3) provides tenant-configurable shaping policies and clear cost/quality tradeoffs.
goals: Define a degradations taxonomy (modes) that can be applied per-tenant and per-route: e.g., soft-throttle, quality-mode downgrades, embeddings-fallback, batch-queueing
Implement tenant shaping policies that enforce a sequence of degradations when capacity pressure crosses thresholds
Expose controls in the Console and API for customers to specify preferred degradations, and provide transparent telemetry and simulated impact before rollout
Maintain core latency SLO for critical routes by sacrificing lower-priority work rather than rejecting requests outright
Provide an audit trail and billing signals for degraded tokens/requests so usage accounting and chargebacks remain accurate
non_goals: Full rewrite of autoscaler — this integrates with existing autoscale signals rather than replacing them
Model-level changes to quality (e.g., retraining models) — we will provide model selector fallbacks, not model retraining
Replacing tenant quota semantics — preserves existing quota/entitlement plumbing
success_metrics: Reduce hard request rejections during capacity pressure by 90% for impacted tenants
Keep p95 latency for critical routes within SLO 95% of the time during degradation windows
Decrease customer-reported incidents related to opaque throttling by 70% in first quarter after launch
At least 80% of active Dedicated tenants adopt or opt into a degradation profile within 6 months (opt-in telemetry)
user_stories: As an engineering lead for a Dedicated tenant, I want to configure a degradation profile that prioritizes real-time chat over batch embeddings so my product remains responsive during spikes.
As an on-call SRE, I want the system to apply progressive degradation automatically when pool utilization exceeds threshold X so I avoid manual evictions during night incidents.
As a platform product manager, I want Console dashboards that show which degradations ran, their duration, and the estimated cost savings so I can explain impact to finance.
As a customer support engineer, I want clear logs and tenant-visible events when a degradation was applied so I can triage customer tickets faster.
requirements: R1 - Degradation Modes: Implement at minimum four distinct degradations: soft-throttle (rate limit low-priority routes), quality downgrade (route-level model variant with lower token cost), fallback-to-embedding-only (for complex gen flows), and deferred-batching (delay noncritical requests into batched windows)
R2 - Policy Engine: New per-tenant policy resource (API + Console) that defines ordered degradations, activation thresholds (utilization, latency, error-rate), and allowed durations
R3 - Triggering Signals: Integrate with runtime signals (pool_cpu/gpu_util, queue_length, p95_latency, preemption_events) to evaluate policy conditions every 10s
R4 - Observable Events: Emit tenant-scoped events when degradations start/stop/mutate including reason, triggered_metric, and estimated tokens impacted
R5 - Cost Accounting: Tag degraded requests in billing pipeline and provide an aggregated cost delta metric per tenant and per degradation window

R6 - Safe Fallbacks: Ensure degradations are monotonic (each step must be reversible and not increase load) and includes a safety cutoff that rejects requests only after all degradation steps have been attempted
R7 - Simulation Mode: Tenant can simulate a degradation policy (dry-run) with synthetic load to see estimated impacts and a preflight report in Console
R8 - API & SDK: Expose policy CRUD via Redwood API and SDKs and allow temporary overrides via request headers for emergency operations

R9 - Backwards Compatibility: Default policy for existing tenants is a conservative profile that prefers soft-throttle and deferred-batching; no tenant should experience new hard rejections by default
R10 - Security & Audit: All policy changes must be audited with actor, timestamp, and justification; policy endpoints must respect RBAC and enterprise SSO controls
acceptance_criteria: AC1 - Create/Update policy: Product API and Console allow creation and update of a tenant degradation policy; changes appear in audit logs
AC2 - Triggering: Under simulated 120% capacity pressure, the runtime applies the tenant policy steps in order and emits start/stop events for each step
AC3 - Latency Preservation: For a critical route marked 'preserve', p95 latency remains within configured SLO in 9/10 test windows where degradations are active
AC4 - Billing Tags: Degraded requests are labeled and show up in billing export with at least three fields: tenant_id, degradation_mode, and tokens_degraded
AC5 - Reversibility: When utilization drops below clear thresholds, all active degradations are removed within 30s and system returns to baseline without data loss
AC6 - Simulation Report: Console dry-run produces a preflight report with estimated percentage of requests impacted and estimated cost delta
AC7 - Safety Cutoff: Under pathological failure (e.g., multiple region failures), system still enforces a final hard-reject after all degradations attempted and document shows how to configure cutoff
AC8 - Observability: Degradation windows are visible in Console timeline with links to trace samples and a synthesized explanation for customer support
dependencies: ENG-78321 - Runtime event bus: reliable tenant-scoped events
ENG-80102 - Billing pipeline: support custom request tags
ENG-81512 - Console: policy editor UI and timeline visualization
ENG-72845 - Autoscaler: expose utilization and preemption signals
DES-3367 - UX: degradation simulation modal and preflight report
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: (1) Internal dogfood in dedicated-alpha pool for 3 weeks with synthetic spike scenarios; (2) Invite-only beta for 10 existing Dedicated customers who opt-in; (3) Gradual enablement for broader Dedicated tenants with default conservative profile and in-console prompts; (4) GA when key SLOs and billing tagging verified. Each phase includes a two-week monitoring window and can be rolled back by disabling policy evaluation on the control plane.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Poorly authored tenant policies could lock out critical traffic. Mitigation: default safe profile, simulation mode, and emergency override header for tenant org admins.
Risk: Billing discrepancies if degraded tokens not captured. Mitigation: integration test suite and reconciliation job to compare pre/post degrade token counts.
Risk: Complexity in operator mental model. Mitigation: Console UX patterns that recommend templates (chat-first, batch-first) and explain tradeoffs with sample numbers.

Risk: Interaction with existing autoscaler causing oscillations. Mitigation: hysteresis windows, evaluation every 10s, and coordination signal to autoscaler team to suppress aggressive scale-downs while degradations active.
notes: This PRD focuses on resident Dedicated capacity. We expect similar semantics could be offered to Hosted in future, but initial scope excludes Hosted. We must coordinate with Billing, Runtime, Console, and Design. Legal to review billing visibility language before GA.
